reason: The narrative depicts extensive collaboration between leaders and the people. The military captains (שָׂרֵי הַמֵּאוֹת) explicitly obey Jehoiada the priest's commands (וַיַּעֲשׂוּ...כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּה). The people of the land (עַם־ הָאָרֶץ) actively participate in multiple coordinated efforts: they gather for the coronation, rejoice together (וַיִּשְׂמַח כָּל־ עַם־ הָאָרֶץ), destroy the temple of Baal together (וַיָּבֹאוּ כָל־ עַם הָאָרֶץ), and escort the king to his palace. Most significantly, Jehoiada establishes a covenant explicitly binding three parties together: YHWH, the king, and the people (בֵּין יְהוָה וּבֵין הַמֶּלֶךְ וּבֵין הָעָם), formalizing their collaborative relationship.
